headline: Big 5 Construct Saudi runs on evening hours across five shows, and that decides how to work it
deck: Four days, five shows, nine conference streams weighted to the first two days, and a venue beside the airport: the practical decisions to make before Riyadh Front opens.
excerpt: Big 5 Construct Saudi opens on Sunday 30 August at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center and runs to Wednesday 2 September, with the halls open from 4pm to 10pm. The floor is not walkable without a shortlist, the conference is front-loaded and the venue rewards planning around the airport rather than the city. This is how to work the four days.
content:
Big 5 Construct Saudi opens on Sunday 30 August at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center and runs to Wednesday 2 September under the patronage of the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources, with the halls open from 4pm to 10pm each day. The organiser expects more than 1,000 exhibitors from over 50 countries and more than 35,000 trade visitors, and the line-up and the patronage are covered in BrentDesk's preview. This piece is about the four days themselves: what the structure of the event means for a visitor with a brief, and the decisions worth making before travelling.

The venue is at ROSHN Front beside King Khalid International Airport, which makes it one of the easier exhibition centres in the Gulf to reach from an inbound flight and one of the less convenient from central Riyadh at rush hour. The evening hours help. Because the halls open at 4pm, a visitor based in the city can work a full day before the drive, but anyone flying in for a single day should plan around the airport in one direction only.

The exhibition covers the early and heavy end of construction rather than the finished product. Its pillars are general construction, concrete, heavy equipment and HVACR, with facilities management alongside them, and each sits in its own co-located show: Heavy Saudi Arabia for equipment and machinery, Totally Concrete Saudi Arabia, HVACR Saudi Arabia, and Saudi FM & Clean for facilities management and cleaning. The theme is From foundation to future, built for every scale, and the halls follow it in sequence from the ground under a building to the contract that runs it.

A floor of that size is not walkable without a shortlist. The organiser publishes the full exhibitor directory online, and reviewing it before travelling is the single most useful hour of preparation, because equipment, concrete, cooling and facilities management are separate buying conversations with separate exhibitors. Treating the event as one exhibition is how visitors lose a day.

The conference programme runs across nine topic areas, from codes and standards to artificial intelligence, concrete, modular construction and HVACR, with sessions on navigating the Saudi Building Code, improving concrete quality, project governance and coordination between HVACR design, installation and facilities management. It is weighted toward the first two days and the tracks run in parallel, so a technical team covering more than one discipline has to split. The speaking organisations and the named speakers are set out in the programme preview.

The Big 5 Impact Trail is the sustainability route through the floor, and it collects the products with published performance numbers: Masdar's Kronospan wood-based panels and engineered boards, Galaxy Technology's Albion Valves with carbon transparency across its cast-iron range, Star Factory's spray polyurethane foam roofing and waterproofing, Keller's ground improvement and foundations, and Al-Futtaim Engineering's integrated facilities management. For anyone whose brief includes embodied carbon it is the efficient way to cover the halls.

Three things are worth deciding in advance. The first is which of the co-located shows a visitor is actually attending, because each is a different buying conversation. The second is whether the conference or the floor is the priority, since the front-loaded programme and the parallel tracks make it hard to do both on the same day. The third is who the visitor needs to meet rather than what they need to see. In a market where the average project award has roughly doubled in size and clients audit local content, the value of an exhibition is in prequalification conversations, and those work better booked than wandered into.

Registration and the visitor guide are on the event website, and the show's accounts on X and Facebook are where programme changes appear first. The market the show opens into is letting fewer and larger packages. The Saudi Contractors Authority recorded 25 awards worth more than SR29.5bn in June, the busiest month of 2026 by count, and expects the value of projects in the Saudi market to exceed SR3 trillion over the next three years. For four days, a large part of the supply chain for that pipeline is in one building.
